column1: # Corrections to the upstream schwa dictionary.
# data/../src/data/schwa-dict.ts is Wikidepia's curated data and is right
# almost everywhere. A row here overrides one word, and needs the same
# evidence any reading needs: a source that marks the pepet vowel, where "ê"
# This diverges from the Python original's `phonemes` output on purpose, so a
# row is a deliberate decision, not a bug fix in passing. Keep it short.
# mask is a hex bitmask over the word's "e"s: bit i set = the i-th "e" is /ə/.

column3: evidence

en.wiktionary marks the adjective and noun "mental" with no pepet, so the common sense (mentality, psychological) is /mental/. Upstream's /məntal/ belongs to the rarer verb sense, to be flung or bounce off. No rule selects that sense: it would need a collocation entry, and there is none, so `mental` always reads /mental/.

Loanword from Dutch "therapie", not ter- + api, so no pepet. The affix rules would otherwise read it as a prefixed root. The rarer superlative tərapi (ter- + rapi) is selected by the part-of-speech resolver instead.
Not se- + rong. Upstream's own test suite asserts /seroŋ/, listing it among the [e] allophones.
Loanword, not te- + knologi. The onset check already rejects it; the row keeps that explicit if the check ever loosens.
Loanword from Dutch "methode", not me- + tode.
Not me- + dan; the common sense is the place name and the field noun, both /medan/.
Not te- + heran; the city, /teheran/. Reached the affix rules once data/indonesian-proper-nouns.tsv kept it from the English table.

column1: # Upstream marks every "e" of these everyday words as pepet. KBBI marks them
# "é" (not pepet), and Bookbot's lexicon agrees through the affixed forms it
# lists (membebek 1, pemerah 1, mencetak 1, berbelok 1, menggendong 1: only
# the prefix vowel is a schwa). Checked against kbbi.web.id, 2026-09-08.

column3: KBBI /bébék/ (duck). Upstream's /bəbəʔ/ contradicts its own membebek and pembebek, which read the root without a schwa.
KBBI /mérah/ (red). Upstream's /mərah/ contradicts pemerah and semerah in the lexicon.
KBBI /bébas/ (free). Upstream's /bəbas/ contradicts pembebas, terbebas and sebebas in the lexicon.
KBBI /cétak/ (print). Upstream's /tʃətaʔ/ contradicts mencetak, pencetak, bercetak and dicetak in the lexicon.
KBBI /bélok/ (turn). Upstream's /bəloʔ/ contradicts membelok and berbelok in the lexicon.
KBBI /lélé/ (catfish). Upstream reads /lələ/.
KBBI /géndong/ (carry on the back). Upstream's /gəndoŋ/ contradicts menggendong in the lexicon.
KBBI /dérék/ (a row; a crane). Upstream's /dərəʔ/ contradicts menderek in the lexicon.
KBBI /pétak/ (a plot, a compartment). Upstream's /pətaʔ/ contradicts berpetak in the lexicon.
KBBI /mémang/ (indeed). The README once held this up as the dictionary being right; it is not. The Jakarta clipping "emang" is /émang/.
KBBI /désa/ (village). As above. Wiktionary marks dèsa and agrees.
An attack, from serang /səraŋ/, which the dictionary, Bookbot and Wiktionary all read with a pepet. The lexicon's own /seraŋan/ contradicts all three; Wiktionary marks sêrangan.
As above: ke- + serang. The lexicon reads /kəseraŋan/.
